title: DR reflection plan: business layer (22 relationship changes)
rationale: Relationship schemas in the business layer that the maintainer-note triage and the sorting-question reflection (cli/scripts/spec-enrich) want removed, renamed, reversed or retargeted. Each operation carries the claims and Clef's sorting answers as evidence and the plan's probability. Accepting an operation means DR applies it with apply-walk.ts; rejecting means the schema stays.

operations.rationale: Rename the predicate of business.businessrole.assigned-to.business.businessprocess to business.businessrole.performs.business.businessprocess. Plan kind rename-predicate, p 0.82; claims node:business.businessprocess#3.

evidence.quote: The businessrole relationships 'assigned-to' and 'performs' toward businessprocess are duplicates expressing the same meaning. Proposed: Keep one of the two relationships and remove the other.

Outcome: alternative (predicate=performs).

Sorting answers (rel:business.businessrole#2): best source of 'assigned-to business.businessprocess': business.businessrole (0.87), business.businessactor (0.04), business.businesscollaboration (0.03); best destination of 'business.businessrole assigned-to': business.businessprocess (0.76), none (0.06), business.businessinteraction (0.05); best predicate: assigned-to (0.74), performs (0.16), none (0.04). operations.rationale: Rename the predicate of business.businessinteraction.serves.business.businessservice to business.businessinteraction.realizes.business.businessservice. Plan kind rename-predicate, p 0.65; claims node:business.businessinteraction#2, rel:business.businessinteraction#1, rel:business.businessinteraction#2.

evidence.quote: The 'serves' relationship from business.businessinteraction to business.businessservice is non-standard because in ArchiMate behavior elements realize services. Proposed: Remove or replace the serves relationship to businessservice with a realizes relationship.

The relationship 'business.businessinteraction serves business.businessservice' is semantically off, because in ArchiMate a business interaction realizes a business service and the service then serves consumers. Proposed: Replace the 'serves' relationship from BusinessInteraction to BusinessService with a 'realizes' relationship.

If a 'realizes' relationship from business.businessinteraction to business.businessservice exists or is intended, the 'serves' relationship between the same pair is redundant with it. Proposed: Remove the 'serves' relationship from BusinessInteraction to BusinessService if a 'realizes' relationship is added.

Outcome: alternative (predicate=realizes).

operations.rationale: Remove business.businessevent.triggers.business.businessfunction: business.businessevent.triggers.business.businessprocess already exists and expresses it. Plan kind retarget, p 0.66; claims rel:business.businessevent#1.

evidence.quote: The triggers relationship from business.businessevent to business.businessfunction is semantically weak because a BusinessFunction has no defined start or sequence, so it should be read as initiating behavior within the function rather than starting the function itself. Proposed: Document that the event triggers behavior within the function, or model the triggered behavior as a process the function contains instead of triggering the function directly.
